phase1.label: INesHeader

regions.summary: iNES header: eight 16-KiB PRG units, thirty-two 8-KiB CHR units, MMC3 mapper 4, no trainer or battery. Header bytes are retained exactly.

phase1.evidence: Packed 4-bit DAC sample record. Direct bank14 callsites independently encode all eight starts; each has delay40/countLE16, stored record size count+3 and adjacent anchored next start. Consumer file0x1EE1C reads delay/count, initializes playback pointer to header+2 (including count-high byte), emits exactly count low/high nibble pairs to $4011, and leaves one stored trailing byte. This implementation detail does not imply count+3 bytes are all played. First seven record ends equal next direct-call start; final end0x4EA9 separates recurring sample nibble pattern from AD0203 code-like content. Generic non-code role of trailing stored byte is supported; exact original sample generator and spoken phrases unresolved. See investigation correction and r001/voice-decoder.json.

regions.summary: Save all fifteen ball-motion bytes, simulate successive three-tick intervals and record eligible actors with arrival-order indices and first-arrival time. FF-delimited assignment filters remove conflicting choices; choose the first remaining actor, defaulting to slot eight and time 0180. Update three fallback destinations, then restore the live motion bytes. regions.summary: When controller bit 10 hex is set, save ten display, scroll and mapper-cache bytes on the stack plus four palette bytes in RAM. Install a temporary display and iterate count/name-NUL/two-big-endian-RAM-pointer records, emitting up to twelve name tiles and one or two hexadecimal RAM values. Marker 80 skips a row; zero ends records. Wait for another controller trigger, then restore the exact saved state in reverse order. The final helper renders high and low nibbles through the sixteen-character digit table. This bounded diagnostic contract does not establish normal gameplay selection.

Marker 80 skips a row; zero ends records. Wait for another controller trigger, then restore the exact saved state in reverse order. The final helper renders high and low nibbles through the sixteen-character digit table. This bounded diagnostic contract does not establish normal gameplay selection.

Preserve the caller's roster partition and finite player-count preconditions; not every stat unit is known.

Emit six-byte transfer descriptors containing destination high/low and four source bytes; advance the PPU destination by one row and update attributes through DBF4 while preserving the source Y cursor. Terminate the descriptor queue with FF. The initial alternate entry returns after installing transfer mode.

regions.summary: Save Y in scratch 14, merge attributes for the current destination and again two tiles to its right, then restore Y. phase1.evidence: Supported direct callers set A=MMC3 sample bank and $04/$05=header pointer. Routine banks A000 window via $ED9B, saves header delay/count in cartridge RAM $6FE7..9, plays low/high nibbles to $4011, advances pointer with bank wrap, decrements exact byte count, restores IRQ/PPU state and returns. Static contract and full loop/return consistency; natural execution not asserted. See voice-decoder.json and static-1ee1c.json.

Derive pixel and screen extents, wrap/clamp limits and palette pointers, then copy sixteen palette bytes into target/current caches. Standalone entry validity requires bootstrap selector one or two and its proven resource-header columns; no natural caller claim follows.

Derive pixel and screen extents, wrap/clamp limits and palette pointers, then copy sixteen palette bytes into target/current caches. Standalone entry validity requires bootstrap selector one or two and its proven resource-header columns; no natural caller claim follows.
